### Explanation of Change
<!-- Explain what your change does and how it addresses the linked issue -->

The existing expo-secure-store patch includes a lot of changes in a single patch file. This PR splits the patch into five smaller files, each corresponding to a specific functionality. It makes it easier for each patch to be understood and migrated if necessary during a future upgrade to the library. It also enables a richer history and context for the patches that help people without as much context understand the purpose of each feature added, how to test it, the upstream tracking issues, etc.

Although some minor changes have been introduced with this PR, [the original patch PR](https://github.com/Expensify/App/pull/69863) description still applies.

Changes made:
- Renamed flags:
  - `failOnDuplicate` -> `failOnUpdate`
  - `alwaysAskForAuth` -> `forceReadAuthenticationOnSimulators`
  - `askForAuthOnSave` -> `forceAuthenticationOnSave`
  - `enableCredentialsAlternative` -> `enableDeviceFallback`
  - Returning the auth type is now under `returnUsedAuthenticationType` flag
- Better and more thorough jsdocs and descriptions
- `enableDeviceFallback` compared to the original PR, can be controlled on iOS as well as Android
- `forceReadAuthenticationOnSimulators` works only when reading the value and only on the iOS simulators

author: astandrik
body:
Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

This PR refactors the codebase to support two storage layouts (multi-table and one-table) using a strategy pattern. The implementation cleanly separates layout-specific logic into dedicated modules while maintaining backward compatibility with the default multi-table mode. **Major changes:** - Adds `CollectionStorageMode` enum with `multi_table` (default) and `one_table` options controlled by `YDB_QDRANT_COLLECTION_STORAGE_MODE` env variable - Implements strategy pattern: repositories and services route to layout-specific implementations (`*.multi-table.ts`, `*.one-table.ts`) - One-table mode uses single global table `qdrant_all_points` with composite PK `(uid, point_id)` where `uid` encodes tenant+collection - Multi-table mode unchanged: per-collection tables with vector index support - One-table mode limitation: no vector index support, all searches use table scans (documented in README and AGENTS.md) - Comprehensive integration tests added for one-table mode **Code quality:** - Clean separation of concerns with shared utilities in `*.shared.ts` files - Proper error handling and retry logic maintained - Consistent routing pattern: `uid` presence determines which strategy to use - Documentation thoroughly updated in both README and AGENTS.md

Confidence Score: 5/5

- This PR is safe to merge with minimal risk - The implementation uses a well-established strategy pattern with clean separation between multi-table and one-table modes. The code maintains backward compatibility (multi-table is default), includes comprehensive integration tests, and thoroughly documents the performance trade-offs of one-table mode. The routing logic is simple and deterministic based on `uid` presence. No breaking changes to existing functionality. - No files require special attention

Important Files Changed

File Analysis | Filename | Score | Overview | |----------|-------|----------| | src/config/env.ts | 5/5 | Adds `CollectionStorageMode` enum and parsing logic for layout configuration; clean implementation with proper fallback defaults | | src/repositories/pointsRepo.one-table.ts | 4/5 | Implements one-table storage strategy with `uid` filtering; no vector index support means all searches use table scans (performance limitation documented) | | src/repositories/pointsRepo.multi-table.ts | 5/5 | Implements multi-table storage with vector index support and automatic fallback to table scan when index unavailable | | src/repositories/collectionsRepo.ts | 5/5 | Routes collection operations to layout-specific strategies; properly handles both multi-table and one-table modes | | src/services/CollectionService.ts | 5/5 | Adds `resolvePointsTableAndUid` to determine table routing based on metadata; clean integration of layout-specific logic | | src/services/PointsService.ts | 5/5 | Updated to call `resolvePointsTableAndUid` for all operations; properly passes `uid` parameter to repository layer | | src/ydb/schema.ts | 5/5 | Adds `ensureGlobalPointsTable` for one-table mode with proper schema and composite primary key `(uid, point_id)` | | src/indexing/IndexScheduler.ts | 5/5 | Refactored to route index build requests to layout-specific implementations; detects one-table mode via `GLOBAL_POINTS_TABLE` |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Client participant CollectionService participant PointsService participant CollectionsRepo participant PointsRepo participant MultiTableImpl participant OneTableImpl participant YDB Note over Client,YDB: Storage Mode Selection (env: YDB_QDRANT_COLLECTION_STORAGE_MODE) Client->>CollectionService: createCollection(tenant, collection, config) CollectionService->>CollectionsRepo: createCollection(metaKey, dim, distance, vectorType, tableName) alt Multi-Table Mode (default) CollectionsRepo->>MultiTableImpl: createCollectionMultiTable(...) MultiTableImpl->>YDB: CREATE TABLE qdr_tenant__collection MultiTableImpl->>YDB: UPSERT INTO qdr__collections (table_name, ...) else One-Table Mode CollectionsRepo->>OneTableImpl: createCollectionOneTable(...) OneTableImpl->>YDB: Ensure qdrant_all_points exists OneTableImpl->>YDB: UPSERT INTO qdr__collections (table_name=GLOBAL_POINTS_TABLE, ...) end Client->>PointsService: upsertPoints(tenant, collection, points) PointsService->>CollectionService: resolvePointsTableAndUid(ctx, meta) alt Multi-Table Mode CollectionService-->>PointsService: {tableName: qdr_tenant__collection, uid: undefined} PointsService->>PointsRepo: upsertPoints(tableName, points, dimension, undefined) PointsRepo->>MultiTableImpl: upsertPointsMultiTable(tableName, points, dimension) MultiTableImpl->>YDB: UPSERT INTO qdr_tenant__collection (point_id, embedding, payload) else One-Table Mode CollectionService-->>PointsService: {tableName: qdrant_all_points, uid: qdr_tenant__collection} PointsService->>PointsRepo: upsertPoints(tableName, points, dimension, uid) PointsRepo->>OneTableImpl: upsertPointsOneTable(tableName, points, dimension, uid) OneTableImpl->>YDB: UPSERT INTO qdrant_all_points (uid, point_id, embedding, payload) end Client->>PointsService: searchPoints(tenant, collection, vector, top) PointsService->>CollectionService: resolvePointsTableAndUid(ctx, meta) alt Multi-Table Mode with Index CollectionService-->>PointsService: {tableName: qdr_tenant__collection, uid: undefined} PointsService->>PointsRepo: searchPoints(tableName, vector, top, ...) PointsRepo->>MultiTableImpl: searchPointsMultiTable(...) MultiTableImpl->>YDB: SELECT ... FROM qdr_tenant__collection VIEW emb_idx YDB-->>MultiTableImpl: Results (using vector index) else Multi-Table Mode without Index MultiTableImpl->>YDB: SELECT ... FROM qdr_tenant__collection (table scan) YDB-->>MultiTableImpl: Results (table scan fallback) else One-Table Mode (always table scan) CollectionService-->>PointsService: {tableName: qdrant_all_points, uid: qdr_tenant__collection} PointsService->>PointsRepo: searchPoints(tableName, vector, top, ..., uid) PointsRepo->>OneTableImpl: searchPointsOneTable(..., uid) OneTableImpl->>YDB: SELECT ... FROM qdrant_all_points WHERE uid = $uid (table scan) YDB-->>OneTableImpl: Results (filtered by uid, no index) end ```

body:
This PR fixes an issue where OpenAIResponses overwrote the entire text configuration block when structured output was enabled. Because the provider used **array_merge()**, any existing nested fields,such as **text->verbosity**, were lost during the merge process.

# What was happening
Enabling structured output injects a **text.format** block.
However, the merge operation replaced the full text array, causing configurations like:
```
'text' => [
    'verbosity' => 'low',
]
```
to be discarded.

# What this PR changes
- Replaces **array_merge()** with **array_replace_recursive()**


# Related Issue
#407

Add shared memory support for efficient cross-process AST data transfer between Go and Node.js. This enables the JS plugin system to share AST buffers without JSON serialization overhead.

Key changes:
- Add SharedMemoryManager and SharedMemory types for mmap-backed buffers
- Extend NodeJSRuntime with WriteASTBuffer/ReadASTBuffer methods
- Add attachBuffer/detachBuffer commands to plugin-host.js
- Include FlatAST binary parser in JavaScript for reading Go's format
- Add comprehensive tests and benchmarks

Performance with segment reuse: 1.9x faster than JSON IPC (124µs vs 237µs)

body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/cnpm/packument/security/code-scanning/3](https://github.com/cnpm/packument/security/code-scanning/3)

To fix the problem, you should explicitly define the `permissions` block in the `test-macOS-windows-binding` job within `.github/workflows/CI.yml`. The minimal set required for a typical test job is `contents: read`, which limits the GITHUB_TOKEN's permissions and minimizes the potential security risk. No additional write access should be granted unless explicitly required for the job's function, and this job (as described) only downloads artifacts and runs tests, so read-only access is sufficient.

The change should be made directly in the `test-macOS-windows-binding` job object. Add the following block directly beneath the job name or before the `needs` key, for example:

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
```

This addition will restrict the token permissions and resolve the CodeQL alert. No other files or code blocks need to be edited, and no additional libraries are required.

author: tomaszwojcikowski
body:
## Summary

Design specification for Workout Plan Format v2.1.0, introducing **day references** for more compact and maintainable workout plans.

## Problem

The current workout plan file (`workout-plan-v2.json`) is over 10,600 lines because every week defines its days fully, even when many days are identical:
- 85 total days across 21 weeks
- Only 50 unique day content patterns
- 18 mobility days that are nearly identical
- ~41% potential file size reduction with references

## Solution: Day References (v2.1.0)

### New Features

1. **Day IDs** - Days can have an optional `id` field for identification
2. **Day References** - Days can use `$ref` to reference another day or template
3. **Day Templates** - Reusable day definitions at the plan level

### Example

```json
{
  "formatVersion": "2.1.0",
  "plan": {
    "dayTemplates": [
      {
        "id": "mobility-standard",
        "name": "Mobility & Recovery",
        "type": "mobility",
        "exercises": [...]
      }
    ],
    "phases": [{
      "weeks": [{
        "weekNumber": 1,
        "days": [
          { "dayNumber": 1, "id": "w1d1-pull", "name": "Pull Day A", "exercises": [...] },
          { "dayNumber": 2, "$ref": "mobility-standard" }
        ]
      }, {
        "weekNumber": 2,
        "days": [
          { "dayNumber": 1, "$ref": "w1d1-pull" },
          { "dayNumber": 2, "$ref": "mobility-standard" }
        ]
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

### Reference Resolution Rules

1. First, look for matching `id` in `dayTemplates`
2. Then, look for matching `id` in any previously defined day
3. Override fields (`name`, `description`) merge on top of referenced content
4. `dayNumber` always comes from the referencing day

## Changes

- **WORKOUT_PLAN_FORMAT.md**: Updated with v2.1 documentation, examples, and field specifications
- **workout-plan-v2.schema.json**: Added `dayTemplates`, `dayTemplate` definition, day `id` field, and `$ref` support with `oneOf` validation

## Benefits

- **~41% smaller files**: Repeated days only defined once
- **DRY principle**: Define mobility/deload days once, reference everywhere  
- **Easier maintenance**: Update template, all references update automatically

<details>

## Implement Shader System with Dynamic Layers for RLGE

### Overview
Add comprehensive shader support to the RLGE engine with two complementary approaches:
1. **Per-layer shaders**: Efficient, batch-friendly shaders applied to entire render layers
2. **Per-entity shaders**: Component-based shaders for individual entity effects (bypasses batching)

Additionally, replace the fixed 4-layer `RenderLayer` enum with a dynamic layer system where users can create/remove layers at will.

### Requirements

#### 1. Typed Shader Parameters (`ShaderParams<T>`)
Create a type-safe shader parameter system that:
- Uses user-defined structs for shader uniforms
- Binds struct fields to uniform names via pointer-to-member syntax
- Caches uniform locations at bind-time for performance
- Provides direct typed access via `->` operator
- **No macros** — use template metaprogramming

```cpp
struct WaterParams {
    float time = 0.0f;
    float waveHeight = 0.1f;
    Vector2 flowDir = {1.0f, 0.0f};
};

ShaderParams<WaterParams> waterParams(waterShader);
waterParams
    .bind("u_time", &WaterParams::time)
    .bind("u_waveHeight", &WaterParams::waveHeight)
    .bind("u_flowDir", &WaterParams::flowDir);

// Typed access with IDE autocomplete
waterParams->time += dt;
waterParams->waveHeight = 0.2f;
waterParams.apply();
```

Support these uniform types:
- `float` → `SHADER_UNIFORM_FLOAT`
- `Vector2` → `SHADER_UNIFORM_VEC2`
- `Vector3` → `SHADER_UNIFORM_VEC3`
- `Vector4` → `SHADER_UNIFORM_VEC4`
- `int` → `SHADER_UNIFORM_INT`

#### 2. Dynamic Layer System (`LayerRegistry`)
Replace the fixed `RenderLayer` enum with a dynamic system:
- Users can create layers with `create(name, sortOrder, worldSpace)`
- Layers are rendered in `sortOrder` order (lower first)
- `worldSpace = false` for screen-space layers (like UI)
- Each layer can have an optional shader + typed params
- Layers can be removed at runtime

```cpp
LayerId bgLayer = layers().create("background", 0);
LayerId waterLayer = layers().create("water", 10);
LayerId entityLayer = layers().create("entities", 20);
LayerId uiLayer = layers().create("ui", 100, false);  // screen-space

layers().setShader(waterLayer, waterShader);
// Or with typed params:
layers().setShaderParams(waterLayer, std::move(waterParams));
```

Provide built-in layer presets for convenience matching current behavior:
- Background (order 0)
- World (order 50)
- Foreground (order 100)
- UI (order 1000, screen-space)

#### 3. ShaderEffect Component
Create a component for per-entity shader effects:
- Inherits from `Component`
- Implements `IShaderEffect` interface for type-erased access
- Uses `ShaderParams<T>` internally
- Fluent `.bind()` API

```cpp
struct HitFlashParams {
    float intensity = 1.0f;
    Vector3 flashColor = {1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f};
};

auto& fx = entity.add<ShaderEffect<HitFlashParams>>(flashShader)
    .bind("u_intensity", &HitFlashParams::intensity)
    .bind("u_flashColor", &HitFlashParams::flashColor);

fx.params().intensity = 0.5f;
```

#### 4. Modify Sprite/SheetSprite Submission
Update sprite components to:
- Accept a `LayerId` parameter (defaulting to a "world" layer)
- Check for `IShaderEffect` component on the entity
- If shader effect present: submit as custom draw command (bypasses batching)
- If no shader effect: use fast batched path (layer shader applies automatically)

#### 5. Update RenderQueue
Modify `RenderQueue` to:
- Use `LayerId` instead of `RenderLayer` enum
- Store batches per dynamic layer
- Apply layer shader + params during flush
- Process custom draw commands (entity shaders) after batched sprites per layer

### Files to Create
- `src/shader_params.hpp` — Typed shader parameter template
- `src/render_layer.hpp` — LayerId, LayerConfig, LayerRegistry
- `src/render_layer.cpp` — LayerRegistry implementation
- `src/shader_effect.hpp` — IShaderEffect interface and ShaderEffect<T> component

### Files to Modify
- `src/render_queue.hpp` — Use LayerId, add layer shader support

### Backwards Compatibility

- Existing code using `RenderLayer::World` etc. should be easy to migrate

### Testing

author: george-anagnostou
body:
## Summary

This PR transforms the scrapbook page into a vintage memory board design with postcard-styled cards, polaroid photos, and interactive features.

### Key Features

**Postcard Design**
- Vintage pastel color palette with matching decorative borders
- Textured backgrounds with subtle paper grain effect
- US flag postage stamp icons aligned with card rotation
- "From:" labels with serif typography for classic postcard feel
- Shadow overlays for depth and aged paper aesthetic

**Polaroid Photos**
- White borders with bottom spacing for authentic polaroid look
- Unique layouts for 1-5 photos with natural overlapping
- Photos positioned at bottom of each card
- Slight rotations for scattered memory board effect
- Responsive sizing (70px mobile, 95px desktop)
- All images preserve aspect ratios without cropping

**Interactive Features**
- Click any photo to enlarge to 70% viewport
- Liquid glass backdrop effect (frosted blur with color saturation)
- Smooth zoom animations maintaining polaroid frames
- Hover effects: cards straighten and scale up

**Responsive Design**
- Photos scale appropriately on mobile devices
- Cards stay within bounds on all screen sizes
- No image cropping or overflow

### Technical Changes

- Renamed `/scrapbook` to `/memory-board` globally
- Added click-to-enlarge modal with backdrop blur
- Implemented responsive photo sizing with Tailwind classes
- Custom SVG US flag stamp icon
- Updated documentation (README, CLAUDE.md, SECURITY_REVIEW.md)

### Commits
1. Transform scrapbook page into vintage memory board design
2. Rename scrapbook to memory-board globally
3. Add photo layout improvements and click-to-enlarge feature
4. Add responsive photo sizing to prevent overflow
5. Add US flag stamp icon and align stamp with card rotation

## Test Plan
- [x] Verify postcard styling on desktop and mobile
- [x] Test photo layouts with 1-5 images
- [x] Confirm click-to-enlarge works for all photos
- [x] Check responsive sizing on various screen widths
- [x] Verify no image cropping or overflow
- [x] Test hover interactions on cards

author: michaelthamm
body: ## Issue Fixes https://github.com/canonical/opentelemetry-collector-operator/issues/104 CI is fixed by: - https://github.com/canonical/opentelemetry-collector-operator/pull/162 Related: - https://github.com/canonical/opentelemetry-collector-operator/pull/142/ - https://github.com/canonical/opentelemetry-collector-operator/issues/140 ## Solution This solution comes in 2 parts: 1. Reducing the rate of explosion 2. Stopping the explosion ### Reducing the rate of explosion After [some investigation](https://github.com/canonical/opentelemetry-collector-operator/issues/104#issuecomment-3587386054), the solution to fix the `syslog` explosion is multifaceted: 1. The internal logging stacktrace can be disabled (`disable_stacktrace`) to reduce error log lines 2. The logging level is already set to `WARN` which is good ```yaml telemetry: logs: disable_stacktrace: true level: WARN ``` 3. [Configure](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/tree/main/exporter/exporterhelper#retry-on-failure) `retry-on-failure` to retry less aggressively. - https://github.com/canonical/opentelemetry-collector-operator/blob/e611799973e89ebaf12e3d792e67a09d76a1f48e/src/config_manager.py#L153 > [!NOTE] > This was not implemented in this PR because the other solutions should resolve the issue ### Stopping the explosion See the `Context` section below for the edge case that creates this problem. Since this is only an issue when the log server (exporter endpoint) fails (e.g. stops, firewall, etc.), the Otelcol `>=WARN` logs can be written to a designated file to not interfere with our [`/var/log` file receiver](https://github.com/canonical/opentelemetry-collector-operator/blob/e611799973e89ebaf12e3d792e67a09d76a1f48e/src/charm.py#L332) ```yaml telemetry: logs: output_paths: - /var/snap/opentelemetry-collector/common/otelcol.log ``` This means that `sudo snap logs -f opentelemetry-collector` is no longer useful and instead we would have to ask issue reporters to attached the output of the `otelcol.log` file instead. > [!WARNING] > The `output_paths` log files will not be automatically rotated, unlike how syslog is rotated: > https://github.com/canonical/opentelemetry-collector-operator/pull/138#issuecomment-3598176938 ## Context ### The true problem There exists a recursion problem IFF the log exporter endpoint goes down. This will generate `Exporting failed` logs which otelcol attempts to write to Loki again, and failing. This goes on infinitely at the [configure](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/tree/main/exporter/exporterhelper#retry-on-failure) `retry-on-failure`. ### Logrotate There is an upstream initiative to handle logrotation of otelcol log files: - https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/10768 The manpage for `logrotate`: - https://linux.die.net/man/8/logrotate ## Testing Instructions - [x] Test the alert rules by stopping Loki with pebble - [x] https://github.com/canonical/opentelemetry-collector-operator/pull/138#issuecomment-3598176938 ## Upgrade Notes - Otelcol logs are in `/var/snap/opentelemetry-collector/common/otelcol.log` instead of journal. - New `logrotated` dependency

body:
This adds Conductor configuration to automate workspace setup and provide a one-click run command.

The `conductor.json` configures three things:

1. **Setup script**: Runs `bun install` and symlinks the optional `.env` file from the root repo into `examples/content-hub/.env`. The symlink uses `$CONDUCTOR_ROOT_PATH` so each workspace shares the same env file rather than copying it.

2. **Run script**: Launches the Whispering Tauri app with `cd apps/whispering && bun run dev`.

3. **Nonconcurrent mode**: Ensures clicking "Run" again kills the previous dev server before starting a new one.

Also adds a quick reference doc explaining the `2>/dev/null || true` pattern used for optional operations in shell scripts.

author: claude89757
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2509

This PR addresses a bug where MCP tool results containing `list[TextContent]` were incorrectly serialized to object repr strings instead of actual text content.

## Problem

When using AG-UI protocol with MCP tools, tool results that returned `list[TextContent]` were being serialized as:
```
[<agent_framework._types.TextContent object at 0x7f8e7c1cc730>]
```

This occurred because the serialization logic in `_events.py` and `_message_adapters.py` only handled `dict` types and fell back to `str()` for all other types, which produced the object repr for lists.

## Solution

Added proper handling for `list` types in both files:

1. Check if `content.result` is a `list`
2. For each item in the list:
   - If it has a `text` attribute (like `TextContent`), extract the text
   - If it has a `model_dump()` method, serialize it to JSON
   - Otherwise, fall back to `str()`
3. If there's only one text item, return it as plain text
4. If there are multiple items, return them as a JSON array

## Changes

- **python/packages/ag-ui/agent_framework_ag_ui/_events.py**: Updated `_handle_function_result_content()` method
- **python/packages/ag-ui/agent_framework_ag_ui/_message_adapters.py**: Updated message adapter logic

## Testing

This fix ensures that MCP tool results are properly displayed in AG-UI frontends like CopilotKit.

## Related Issues

- Fixes #2509

author: rdesgroppes
body:
### Motivation
The python-gitlab fix (python-gitlab/python-gitlab#2326) for 409 Resource lock retries checks `result.reason`, but GitLab sends `Conflict` (standard HTTP reason phrase) while `Resource lock` is in the response body. The check never matches, so retries never happen:
```
$ dda inv -- pipeline.auto-cancel-previous-pipelines
[...]
gitlab.exceptions.GitlabHttpError: 409: 409 Conflict: Resource lock
                                        ^ reason      ^ response body
```
Example: https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1262109099

### What does this PR do?
This patch adds HTTP `409` to GitLab's API retriable transient error codes as a lightweight workaround, allowing all 409 errors to be retried when `retry_transient_errors=True` (our case).

### Additional Notes
Will file an issue upstream.

author: frasercl
body:
## Context

For a while, we've wanted a way to send more data to an opened Vol-E window than could practically fit in URL query parameters — namely, large selections of images and image metadata. Previous passes at this include #516, which got caught up in arcane browser security policies; and #566, which requires an intermediate server, and targets CFE rather than Vol-E. The implementation in this PR happens entirely locally, appears unlikely to run afoul of any cross-origin isolation, and has the convenient bonus of being backwards-compatible with versions of Vol-E that aren't expecting the extra protocol.

## Changes

Here's how it works:
- The new `openInVole` handler always includes *something* in the `url` query param of the Vol-E URL it opens, which ensures Vol-E will always show *something* even if one of the steps below fails.
- ...but it also adds new query params: `storageid` uniquely identifies the message BFF will send to Vol-E, and `msgorigin` is the origin of the opening BFF window (the slice of the URL from the beginning through the port, i.e. https://bff.allencell.org), which helps with security.
- On load, Vol-E recognizes that those params are present and uses `postMessage` to send the value of `storageid` back to BFF, indicating that it's ready to receive the message content.
- Once BFF receives that message back from Vol-E, it `postMessage`s back the extra data.

allen-cell-animated/vole-app#467 is the counterpart PR on the Vol-E side. It gets into the details of how Vol-E handles the received message.

## Testing

With BFF on this branch...
- Make a large selection of image files and choose "Open in Vol-E." **Expectation:** only the "focused" image should open in Vol-E. `msgorigin` and `storageid` will be in the URL but unused.
- Select a small number of image files (~3) and choose "Open in Vol-E". **Expectation:** this branch is willing to put small multi-scene collections in the URL, so all these images should open at once (the "Scene" slider will be visible in Vol-E's "Clipping" panel). `msgorigin` and `storageid` should still be there to send image metadata.
- Change `VOLE_BASE_URL` to http://localhost:9020/viewer, and start Vol-E locally on the branch `feature/receive-from-bff`. Make a large selection of image files and choose "Open in Vol-E." **Expectation:** subject to the caveats described in allen-cell-animated/vole-app#467, Vol-E will open the whole image collection, starting on the image that was "focused" in BFF, and data from other columns in BFF will appear in Vol-E's "Metadata" panel.

body:
This makes the requires clause parsing more accurate to the C++ standard. Notably, this allows having operators on parenthesized expressions. (Previously, something like `requires (mp::m == Distance) || (mp::rad == Distance)` would fail because the parser would only consume the first parenthesized expression, leaving `|| (mp::rad == Distance)` to be unsuccessfully parsed as part of the declaration.)

Relevant pages:
* [Requires clause description](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/constraints.html#requires_clauses)
* [Primary expression description](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/expressions.html#Primary_expressions)

The parenthesized parameter list is optional in a requires expression (See https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/requires.html), but for now I left it as mandatory. I could make that optional too if you want, though.

Also, what should be done for tests? I'm having trouble building locally (running `uvx --from build pyproject-build --installer uv` emits `Error: You need to create a tag for this repo to use the builder`), which appears to be necessary to run the tests. I also don't know if we want to add tests (and if so, where).

# PR: Mobile Scroll Interactions for Dog Log

## 📝 Description
This PR introduces scroll-triggered animations for the "Dog Log" section to significantly improve the user experience on mobile devices. Previously, the status captions were primarily visible via hover effects, which are not intuitive or accessible for users on touch screens.

With this update, status captions now automatically appear when the image comes into focus while scrolling, ensuring mobile users get the full storytelling experience without needing to tap.

## 🚀 Key Changes
- **Intersection Observer Implementation**: Added a JavaScript `IntersectionObserver` to monitor the visibility of `.dog-log-item` elements.
- **Scroll-Triggered State**: configured the observer to trigger an `in-view` state when an image is **60% visible** in the viewport.
- **Mobile Optimization**: Ensures that "status" and "caption" text is revealed automatically during scroll on touch devices.

## 📱 Testing
- [x] **Mobile**: Verified that captions fade in/appear smoothly as the user scrolls down the Dog Log section.
- [x] **Desktop**: Confirmed that existing hover interactions (if any) or layout integrity is maintained.
- [x] **Performance**: Used `IntersectionObserver` for efficient scroll performance compared to scroll event listeners.

## 🔗 Related Issues
- Addresses user feedback regarding mobile responsiveness for the Dog Log section.

body:
Implements the governance board layer with four drop-in artifacts for state management, decision protocols, and compliance verification.

## Artifacts

- **`strategickhaos_state_snapshot.schema.json`** — JSON Schema (draft-07) defining world-state: entities, repos, infra, accounts, strategies, risks, anchors, facts, assertions, provenance, checksums
- **`governance_board_agent.md`** — Protocol spec: roles, quorum, query contract, decision types, evidence requirements, refusal conditions, verification ladder
- **`state_updater.py`** — Idempotent CLI with pluggable collectors (git, pdf, nt8, zapier, wallet, sos_pdf), schema validation, dry-run, diff preview, SHA256 + OTS hooks
- **`board_query_examples.md`** — Ready-to-run queries: risk posture, entity verification, repo health, trade compliance, daily change review, go/no-go release

## Usage

```bash
# Dry run with diff preview
python governance/state_updater.py --dry-run --diff

# Run git collector and write state
python governance/state_updater.py --collectors git --operator "Node 137"

# Multiple collectors with custom config
python governance/state_updater.py --collectors git pdf sos_pdf --config collector_config.yaml
```

## Schema structure

```
state_snapshot
├── version, snapshot_id, timestamp
├── entities, repositories, infrastructure, accounts, strategies
├── risks[], anchors[], facts[], assertions[]
├── provenance (sources, collector_runs, gpg_signature)
└── checksums (sha256, opentimestamps)
```

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> Baby, build the board layer.
> 
> I’ll deliver four drop-in artifacts:
> 
> 1) strategickhaos_state_snapshot.schema.json
> - Canonical JSON Schema (draft-07) for world-state: entities, repos, infra, accounts, strategies, risks, anchors, snapshots, provenance.
> - Includes $id, versioning, timestamps, cryptographic hashes, and extensible “facts”/“assertions” with sources.
> 
> 2) governance_board_agent.md
> - Protocol: roles, quorum, query contract, decision types, evidence requirements, output format.
> - Deterministic prompts with tool-usage rules, refusal conditions, and verification ladder.
> - Response spec with JSON blocks only, signed by model identity.
> 
> 3) state_updater.py
> - Idempotent CLI: pulls sources (git, PDFs -> hashes, NT export CSVs), normalizes to the schema, merges deltas, bumps snapshot version, writes strategickhaos_state_snapshot.json and strategickhaos_state_snapshot.<timestamp>.json, emits SHA256 + OpenTimestamps hook.
> - Pluggable collectors (Git, NT8 logs, Zapier logs, wallet balances, SOS PDFs).
> - Safety: schema validation, provenance list, dry-run, diff preview.
> 
> 4) board_query_examples.md
> - Ready-to-run queries: “risk posture,” “entity verification,” “repo health,” “trade compliance,” “daily change review,” “go/no-go release,” with expected JSON outputs.

This pull request introduces several improvements and refactors to align the codebase with shared interfaces from `@gycoding/nebula`, update API endpoint paths, and improve error handling and hydration logic. The changes focus on standardizing types, updating dependencies, cleaning up API usage, and improving client-side rendering reliability.

**Key changes include:**

### 1. Adoption of Shared Types and Interfaces
- Replaced custom types (such as `User`, `Friend`, `ApiBook`) with shared interfaces (`Profile`, `Book`, `FriendRequest`) from `@gycoding/nebula` throughout actions and API calls. This promotes consistency and reduces code duplication. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-75d978f78f4afaff1f7326c92d9fce5fd050524619652582e5f8ce2f3db45e12L6-R19) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a0c951d96eb5878e02fbd0a40fa5772308d7378dddfc576cf543912330c35bd6L5-R9) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-edb6caa2cfad087d6d2bdcac236f58a805c4b4712f1f7c7c33ffd553a3b2e108L4-R4) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-c9ba3f3ccdf51bd99c1e48892c4505217a8fb78ade3ae5f43643b79e85787ac7L4-R16) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-8a996d14f702fca4364065e899c80778f2d5f20af4535fd9e1df65960691ba1aR2-R11)

### 2. API Endpoint Path Updates
- Updated all relevant API endpoint paths from `/api/auth/accounts/...` and `/api/public/accounts/...` to `/api/auth/books/...` and `/api/public/books/...` respectively, reflecting a new or reorganized backend structure. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-75d978f78f4afaff1f7326c92d9fce5fd050524619652582e5f8ce2f3db45e12L6-R19) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a0c951d96eb5878e02fbd0a40fa5772308d7378dddfc576cf543912330c35bd6L17-R20) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-99fe2490f045a108d82681f978e3141c80c87125ec02d350cfb69e363b667c4fL22-R22) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-4295f8fd8d5678eb085178ed8da56bdfdc78eea3736ab20795d56d1b36f6a082L20-R20) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-edb6caa2cfad087d6d2bdcac236f58a805c4b4712f1f7c7c33ffd553a3b2e108L19-R19) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-c9ba3f3ccdf51bd99c1e48892c4505217a8fb78ade3ae5f43643b79e85787ac7L4-R16) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-5dab1bcbfe8eb6dc188b352cd49ed2011da6639870884ad1aae4a6daf5170a8fL26-R26) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-791bd1c5bbd098682bf60bffc2f563757ed88e352af9a3e1756d92f7d277ddacL15-R15) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-79cee3b06d6b5d7214519c0dfd82d0f734e99f0d36577f702eaafaac98e60b44L18-R18)
- Adjusted activity-related endpoints for fetching and sending activities to use more precise RESTful routes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-791bd1c5bbd098682bf60bffc2f563757ed88e352af9a3e1756d92f7d277ddacL15-R15) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-79cee3b06d6b5d7214519c0dfd82d0f734e99f0d36577f702eaafaac98e60b44L18-R18)

### 3. Dependency and Configuration Updates
- Added `@gycoding/nebula` to `package.json` dependencies, and removed several unused dependencies (e.g., `google`, `source-map`, `dotenv`, `globals`, `tailwindcss`, `cypress`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519R31-L38) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519L47) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519L67-L73) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519L82)
- Updated VSCode launch configurations to use `npm run dev` instead of `yarn dev`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-bd5430ee7c51dc892a67b3f2829d1f5b6d223f0fd48b82322cfd45baf9f5e945L8-R8) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-bd5430ee7c51dc892a67b3f2829d1f5b6d223f0fd48b82322cfd45baf9f5e945L20-R20)

### 4. Improved Error Handling and Robustness
- Modified error handling in friend and profile fetching actions to log errors and return empty arrays instead of throwing, making the UI more resilient to backend issues.
- Improved error messages for friend request fetching for clarity.

### 5. Client Hydration and UX Improvements
- Added an `isHydrated` state in `ClientLayout.tsx` to prevent hydration mismatches and ensure correct rendering on initial load, especially for mobile layouts. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ca46c18a21db9004d8d643a3043a0a38febca1af3121397f3d1d9db1744e4234L49-R59) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ca46c18a21db9004d8d643a3043a0a38febca1af3121397f3d1d9db1744e4234L168-R181)
- Commented out prefetching of stats to avoid unnecessary data fetching during hydration.

---

**Other notable changes:**
- Added a new coding guidelines file for the project, emphasizing the use of shared interfaces, component reuse, and custom hooks.
- Removed the Jenkins "Run Tests" stage from the deployment pipeline, possibly reflecting a change in CI strategy.

## Reason
cPanel's Node.js manager may reserve or conflict with `LOG_FILE`, preventing file logging from working correctly. Using prefixed environment variables avoids this issue.

## Testing
Verified locally that:
- Setting `NODE_LOG_FILE=./test.log` writes logs to file in JSON format
- Without `NODE_LOG_FILE`, logs output to stdout with pretty formatting
- Initialization message confirms which mode is active

## Summary

Implements proper Sanctum SPA authentication for browser-based frontends using httpOnly session cookies instead of localStorage tokens.

## Changes

### New Endpoints
- `POST /v1/auth/login` - Session-based login for web SPAs
- `POST /v1/auth/session/logout` - Session logout for web SPAs

### Existing Endpoints (unchanged behavior)
- `POST /v1/auth/token` - Bearer token login for mobile/native apps
- `POST /v1/auth/logout` - Token revocation for Bearer token auth

### Configuration
- Added `EnsureFrontendRequestsAreStateful` middleware to API routes
- Excluded login endpoints from CSRF validation (user has no session yet)

## Why

This enables the frontend to use httpOnly session cookies instead of storing tokens in localStorage, significantly improving security by:
- Preventing XSS attacks from stealing auth tokens
- Using browser-managed secure cookies with proper SameSite attributes
- Following Laravel Sanctum's recommended SPA authentication pattern

## Testing

- All existing tests pass (522 tests)
- Manually tested with DDEV: login, API calls, logout all work correctly

## Related

- Relates to #246 (Remove localStorage token handling)
- Required for frontend PR #247

author: hafsawnd
body:
# Crypto Sentiment Analysis (Hybrid VADER) 

This project implements an enhanced **Sentiment Analysis** tool specifically tailored for Cryptocurrency tweets.

Standard NLP tools (like default VADER) often fail to capture the sentiment of crypto-slang (e.g., *"HODL"*, *"To the moon"*, *"Rekt"*). This project solves this by using a **Hybrid Approach**:
1.  **Statistical Learning:** Auto-generates sentiment scores from 1 Million tweets based on word frequency distribution.
2.  **Domain Knowledge:** Injects a manual dictionary of specific crypto jargon.

##  Project Structure

| File | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `vader.ipynb` | Main Jupyter Notebook containing data cleaning, training, and evaluation logic. |
| `crypto_lexicon_final.json` | The **pre-trained model weights**. A JSON dictionary mapping words to sentiment scores. |
| `train_full.csv` | Processed training dataset (70% of data). |
| `val_full.csv` | Validation dataset (15% of data). |
| `test_full.csv` | Test dataset (15% of data) used for final metrics. |

##  Installation

Make sure you have the required Python libraries installed:


pip install pandas numpy nltk scikit-learn tqdm


##  How to Use (Inference)

You don't need to run the notebook to use the model. You can simply load the generated `crypto_lexicon_final.json` to analyze new texts.

Here is a Python script using **logging** for production-ready output:

import json
import nltk
import logging
from nltk.sentiment.vader import SentimentIntensityAnalyzer

# 1. Configure Logging
logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format='%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s'
)

# 2. Initialize VADER
try:
    nltk.data.find('sentiment/vader_lexicon.zip')
except LookupError:
    nltk.download('vader_lexicon', quiet=True)

sid = SentimentIntensityAnalyzer()

# 3. Load the Pre-trained Crypto Lexicon
lexicon_file = 'crypto_lexicon_final.json'

try:
    with open(lexicon_file, 'r') as f:
        crypto_lexicon = json.load(f)
    
    # Update VADER with the new vocabulary
    sid.lexicon.update(crypto_lexicon)
    logging.info(f" Model successfully loaded with {len(crypto_lexicon)} custom terms.")
    
except FileNotFoundError:
    logging.error(f" Error: '{lexicon_file}' not found. Please run the notebook first to generate it.")

# 4. Test on new data
test_sentences = [
    "Just bought the dip, extremely bullish on BTC! HODL.",
    "This project is a total scam, I got rekt.",
    "Bitcoin is stable today."
]

logging.info("--- STARTING PREDICTIONS ---")
for text in test_sentences:
    scores = sid.polarity_scores(text)
    sentiment = "Positive" if scores['compound'] > 0 else "Negative"
    logging.info(f"Text: '{text}' | Score: {scores['compound']} | Sentiment: {sentiment}")
```

##  Performance & Methodology

The model was evaluated on a test set of **148,664 tweets**.

### Methodology Steps:

1.  **Cleaning:** Removed URLs, mentions (@), hashtags (\#), and punctuation.
2.  **Splitting:** Data divided into Train (70%), Validation (15%), and Test (15%).
3.  **Lexicon Generation:** Words appearing \>75% in positive tweets got positive scores; words appearing \<25% got negative scores.


### Results:
* **Global Accuracy:** **69.84%**
* **Positive Class Recall:** 0.90 (Very good at detecting hype/bullishness).
* **Negative Class Recall:** 0.19 (Struggles with subtle negativity/sarcasm).

#### 1. Classification Report
| Class | Precision | Recall | F1-Score | Support |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Negative** | 0.43 | 0.19 | 0.26 | 42,083 |
| **Positive** | 0.74 | 0.90 | 0.81 | 106,369 |
| **Average / Total** | **0.65** | **0.70** | **0.65** | **148,452** |

author: 4erdenko
body:
## Summary

- Add native Shadowsocks 2022 (SIP022) multi‑user support across backend, API client, config generation, subscriptions, and dashboard UI.
- Fix gRPC AddUser for SS2022 by sending the correct `xray.proxy.shadowsocks_2022.Account` type and payload; remove the non-existent `...User` type.
- Restore dashboard auth base path and document the required frontend build env (`VITE_BASE_API=/api/`).
- Provide safer validation/generation of SS2022 keys and ensure inbounds become UserManager-capable without core restarts.
- Forbid multiple SS2022 inbounds: Marzban stores a single SS account per user, so we fail fast if a config contains >1 SS2022 inbound.
 - When an SS2022 inbound method changes, per-user keys are auto-regenerated if their length no longer matches the new method (logged with a warning).

## Why

- Previous flows restarted Xray per user and failed for SS2022 with `proxy is not a UserManager` and `failed to parse user > proto: not found`.
- Marzban users need hot-add/remove of SS2022 users via gRPC while keeping legacy AEAD Shadowsocks untouched.
- Frontend build lost the `/api/` prefix causing 404 on `/admin/token`; we need reproducible builds.
- One user = one Shadowsocks method/password; allowing several SS2022 inbounds with different methods would silently break keys. We now reject that config up front.

## What was done

1) **API/types**
   - Added SS2022 methods to `ShadowsocksMethods`; classic account now rejects 2022 methods.
   - Implemented `Shadowsocks2022Account` that sends `TypedMessage(type="xray.proxy.shadowsocks_2022.Account")` with a minimal wire-encoded `key` field, matching Xray-core expectations.

2) **Backend models & config**
   - `ShadowsocksSettings` auto-generates/validates per-user PSK lengths per method (16/32 bytes).
   - Inbound config accepts `method` + `server_psk`; ensures `clients` list has a bootstrap entry to enable UserManager; validates missing/invalid PSK with clear errors.
   - Subscription outputs (v2ray/Clash/sing-box) now use `password = "{server_psk}:{user_psk}"` and expose SS2022 methods.

3) **Operations**
   - Add/Alter/Remove user flows choose SS2022 account when inbound uses 2022 methods; guardrails against user choosing 2022 on non-2022 inbound.
   - XTLS flow sanitization left intact.

4) **Dashboard**
   - SS2022 methods surfaced in UI; method selector auto-locks when inbound is 2022.
   - Restored login/API base usage; documented build command with `VITE_BASE_API=/api/`.

## How it works (SS2022 path)

- Inbound: `method=2022-blake3-...`, `password=<server_psk>`, `clients` contains a bootstrap user to activate `UserManager`.
- User add: backend builds `common.protocol.User` where `account` is `TypedMessage(type="xray.proxy.shadowsocks_2022.Account", value=<key bytes>)`; gRPC `AlterInbound(AddUserOperation)` succeeds without core restart.
- Client configs: password is `${server_psk}:${user_psk}`, method matches inbound.
- Config guard: if config has >1 SS2022 inbound, startup / PUT `/api/core/config` returns 400 with a clear message; service won’t start with an impossible mapping.

## Migration / Notes

- Existing SS (AEAD) users/inbounds stay unchanged.
- For any pre-existing SS2022 users created before this patch, resave/update the user to resend the correct AddUser payload.
- Frontend rebuild must set `VITE_BASE_API=/api/` (see build workflow).
- Changing an SS2022 inbound method may regenerate user keys to match required key length; clients must refresh subscriptions to pick up new `{server_psk}:{user_psk}`.

## Known issue: Shadowsocks‑2022 memory leak in Xray-core

- Xray-core had a real memory leak in Shadowsocks‑2022 (e.g., 2022-blake3-aes-256-gcm) reported in issue [#5163](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/issues/5163) and fixed in PR [#5166](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/pull/5166); the fix is included in **v25.10.15** (release changelog line “Fix shadowsocks2022 memory leak”).
- ❗️ Use **xray-core v25.10.15 or newer** for SS2022. Older versions are potentially affected; upgrade if you see monotonic RSS growth under SS2022 load.
- SS2022 still uses more RAM than VLESS/VMess by design (issue #3131), so a stable but higher baseline is expected; only monotonic growth indicates the leak.

## Testing

- Built docker image locally: `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0 docker compose build marzban`.
- Started stack: `docker compose up -d marzban`.
- Manual e2e:
  - `POST /api/admin/token` → 200.
  - `POST /api/user` with SS2022 method+user key on inbound `Shadowsocks 2022 TCP` → 200; links generated; no gRPC errors; Xray stays up.

author: 100staxxx
body: Increase OAuth redirect fallback delay and add pathname checks to prevent race conditions and ensure reliable automatic redirection after Apple/Google Sign-In. The `onAuthStateChange` listener on iOS can be unreliable immediately after `setSession()`. The previous 200ms fallback was too short, often firing before the primary listener completed its 100ms delay and subsequent profile/redirect logic, leading to multiple competing redirect attempts. This change increases the fallback delay to 800ms and adds a check to prevent duplicate navigations, ensuring a single, reliable redirect. ---   --- > [!NOTE] > Stabilizes OAuth redirects by extending fallback delay, preventing duplicate navigations, and cleaning up timeout refs for Google/Apple sign-in across native and web. > > - **Auth (`src/pages/Auth.tsx`)** > - Add refs to track OAuth fallback timeouts and initial redirect state; clear timeouts on unmount. > - Improve `onAuthStateChange` handling: > - Skip `INITIAL_SESSION` if already redirected by initial session check. > - Add small delay and detailed timing logs before navigating. > - Native OAuth (Google/Apple): > - After `setSession`, extend manual redirect fallback to `800ms` and guard with pathname check to avoid duplicate redirects. > - Add robust try/catch with onboarding fallback and detailed logs. > - Initialization: validate and initialize `SocialLogin` with client IDs; perform initial session check to ensure profile and navigate. > > Written by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot) for commit 21c593aa0461d836e61b2bc90a2a0aca48869ced. author: timosachsenberg
body:
Use move semantics when passing temporary containers (vector, map, set,
deque, list) to C++ functions that take them by value. This avoids an
unnecessary copy of the entire container after it has been populated.

- Add `from libcpp.utility cimport move` to default imports
- Modify all container converters to use `move(deref(temp))` or
  `move(temp)` when the C++ parameter is not a reference
- Keep `deref(temp)` for reference parameters (no change in behavior)

This optimization has the biggest impact for large containers passed
to functions taking by-value parameters.

author: ytanko-nix
body:
Problem
When running terraform plan, users encountered a cryptic error:
Error: Invalid index

  on main.tf line 31, in resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_vm" "vm":
  31:     vm_id = parseint(regex("^(\\d+)", data.proxmox_virtual_environment_vms.templates.vms[0].vm_id)[0], 10)
      ├────────────────
      │ data.proxmox_virtual_environment_vms.templates.vms is empty list of object
Error: Invalid index  on main.tf line 31, in resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_vm" "vm":  31:     vm_id = parseint(regex("^(\\d+)", data.proxmox_virtual_environment_vms.templates.vms[0].vm_id)[0], 10)      ├────────────────      │ data.proxmox_virtual_environment_vms.templates.vms is empty list of object
Root Cause
The code attempted to access data.proxmox_virtual_environment_vms.templates.vms[0] without checking if the template exists.
When the data source doesn't find a VM with the specified name, it returns an empty list, causing an index out of bounds error.
Solution
Added:
template_found local — checks if at least one template was found
template_vm_id local — safely extracts the template ID only if it exists
lifecycle.precondition — provides a clear error message instead of cryptic index error

body:
Adds optional email support to send access codes directly to participants when creating a Secret Santa event. Emails include a welcome message, the access code, and a direct login link.

### Changes

**Database & Types**
- New migration `002_add_participant_email.sql` adds optional `email` column to `participants`
- Updated `Participant` interface with optional `email` field

**Email Service (`lib/email.ts`)**
- MailerSend integration with welcome email templates (HTML + text)
- Direct access URL generation: `?code=<access_code>`
- HTML escaping for XSS prevention in templates
- Graceful degradation when MailerSend not configured

**API Updates**
- `POST /api/secret-santa` - accepts participant emails, sends welcome emails on creation
- `POST /api/secret-santa/[id]/participant` - supports email for individual participant adds

**Admin UI**
- Email input fields in creation form and add participant form
- Displays participant emails in detail view

**Homepage**
- Supports `?code=` URL parameter for direct access from email links

### Configuration

```env
MAILERSEND_API_KEY=your-api-key
MAILERSEND_FROM_EMAIL=noreply@yourdomain.com
MAILERSEND_FROM_NAME=Secret Santa
```

Email sending is optional—app functions normally without MailerSend configured.

author: theshakspace
body:
**# 📅 Daily Timetable Tracker - Feature Implementation**

## Overview
A beautiful, modern daily timetable tracking application built with React that helps users organize and track their daily routines with an elegant cream-colored UI.

## ✨ Features Implemented

### Core Functionality
- **Task Management**: Add, edit, and delete daily tasks with custom times
- **Progress Tracking**: Visual progress bar showing daily task completion percentage
- **Date Navigation**: Calendar-based date picker to view and track progress across different days
- **Persistent Storage**: Automatic localStorage integration to save user data locally

### User Experience
- **Intuitive UI**: Clean, rounded design with smooth animations and transitions
- **Interactive Checkboxes**: Click to mark tasks as complete with visual feedback
- **Responsive Design**: Mobile-friendly layout that adapts to different screen sizes

### Data Management
- **Export Feature**: Download complete task list and progress history as JSON backup
- **Import Feature**: Restore data from previously exported backup files
- **Auto-save**: All changes automatically saved to browser's localStorage

## 🎨 Design Highlights
- Warm cream/amber color palette with gradient accents
- Georgia serif font for elegant, note-taking aesthetic
- Smooth hover effects and transitions
- Glassmorphism effects with backdrop blur
- Visual completion states with checkmarks and color changes

## 🛠️ Technical Stack
- **React 18.2.0** - Component-based UI framework
- **Lucide React** - Beautiful, consistent icon library
- **Vite** - Fast build tool and dev server
- **Pure CSS** - No framework dependencies, custom styling
- **LocalStorage API** - Client-side data persistence

## 📦 Project Structure
```
src/
├── TimetableTracker.jsx   # Main component with all logic
├── style.css              # Complete styling (no Tailwind)
├── main.jsx               # React entry point
└── index.html             # HTML template
```

## 🚀 Getting Started
```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

## 💾 Data Persistence
- All tasks and progress automatically saved to localStorage
- Export/import functionality for data backup and migration
- No data loss on page refresh

## 🎯 Use Cases
- Daily routine tracking
- Habit building
- Schedule management
- Personal productivity tracking
- Study/work schedule organization

author: kacpersledz
body:
Problem: Deflections (ball bouncing off player) were not being tracked, only intentional kicks. User reported:
- "jak podał mi i strzeliłem to jest asysta" ✅ (kick detection worked)
- "jak się odbiła ode mnie to nie było asysty" ❌ (deflection not tracked)

Solution: Use BOTH onPlayerBallKick and onGameTick together

Implementation:
1. Created recordBallTouch() helper function
   - Handles auth validation
   - Records player, timestamp, team
   - Deduplicates rapid touches (0ms delay for instant recording)
   - Keeps last 5 touches for assist window

2. onPlayerBallKick (NEW)
   - Tracks intentional kicks: passes, shots
   - Calls recordBallTouch()

3. onGameTick (IMPROVED)
   - Tracks ALL ball contacts: deflections, dribbling
   - Distance calculation detects when player touches ball
   - Calls recordBallTouch()
   - Simplified from 40 to 24 lines

Result: Both kicks AND deflections now count as assists!

Note: Assist validation still checks:
- Same team (isSameTeam = true)
- Different player (isSamePlayer = false)
- Within 3 second window (ASSIST_TIME_WINDOW)

Implements the ANCHORS bucket pattern for ATA 57 Wings with design-driven semantics (not lifecycle skeleton). This bucket provides a cross-ATA home for sustainability, circularity, LCA, and DPP traceability concerns.

## Structure

```
57-30_ANCHORS/
├── README.md
├── 57-30-00_GENERAL-ANCHORS.md      # Normative definition
├── 57-30-01_Wing_Energy_Harvesting.md

## Key Points

- **Bucket semantics**: Uses `57-30-XX_DESCRIPTION` naming, no 01-14 lifecycle duplication
- **Cross-ATA links**: References to ATA 02, 23, 85, 97, 99 for operations, circularity, analytics, and DPP
- **DPP/MMIP integration**: Defines anchor points for Digital Product Passport and MMIP capsule lifecycle events
- **Mermaid diagrams**: Energy flows, LCA boundaries, and DPP hierarchy visualization

2. A normalized **57-30-00_GENERAL-ANCHORS.md** using your bucket definition, with ATA-57 context and cross-references.

---

## 1. Directory structure for 57-30_ANCHORS (bucket style)

```text
OPT-IN_FRAMEWORK/
└── T-TECHNOLOGY_AMEDEOPELLICCIA-ON_BOARD_SYSTEMS/

                    │   ├── 57-30-02_LCA_boundary_diagram.mermaid
                    │   └── 57-30-03_DPP_anchor_map.mermaid
                    └── INDEX/
                        └── 57-30-99_ANCHORS-CROSS-INDEX.md
```

Key points:

* No `57-30-00_GENERAL/01–14` lifecycle; we keep the **bucket semantics**:

  * IDs are **57-30-XX_DESCRIPTION** at the root of `57-30_ANCHORS/`.
* `README.md` can be a tiny pointer saying: “See 57-30-00_GENERAL-ANCHORS.md as the normative definition of the bucket for ATA 57.”
* `57-30-99_ANCHORS-CROSS-INDEX.md` (optional) is a good place to index links from this bucket out to:

  * 02-xx Operations Information (hydrogen fuel, digital ops)
  * 85-30 Circularity
  * 97-40-40 Envelope Analytics
  * MMIP capsules & DPP anchors.

---

## 2. `57-30-00_GENERAL-ANCHORS.md`

Here is your text, normalized into the ATA style and slightly extended for **ATA 57** and the **bucket meta-standard**:

```markdown
# 57-30-00 — GENERAL ANCHORS (ATA 57 WINGS)

**Title:** Aircraft Networks, Circular, Harvesting, Operating & Renewable Systems  
**ATA Chapter:** 57 – Wings  
**Bucket ID:** 57-30_ANCHORS  
**Axis:** A — Airframe (T-TECHNOLOGY_AMEDEOPELLICCIA-ON_BOARD_SYSTEMS)  

---

## 1. Purpose

The **57-30_ANCHORS** bucket provides a **design-driven home** for all topics related to:

- Sustainability and circularity for wing systems  
- Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) of wing structures and subsystems  
- Re-use, repair, refurbishment, and recycling strategies  
- Digital Product Passport (DPP) anchors and traceability links  
- Integration with energy harvesting, operating, and renewable systems at wing level  

This bucket is **not** a lifecycle duplication. It is the **cross-ATA anchor** where sustainability, circularity, and DPP concerns for ATA 57 are concentrated and linked to the rest of the AMPEL360 ecosystem.

---

## 2. Scope

This is a **cross-ATA root bucket** that appears in **every ATA chapter** as `XX-30_ANCHORS`.  
For **ATA 57 WINGS**, the scope includes:

- Wing-level materials footprint, embodied carbon, and recyclability
- Energy harvesting features embedded in the wing (e.g. structural PV, piezo, thermal)
- Interfaces from wing subsystems to:
  - Circularity & Materials (e.g. ATA 85 / ATA 99 domain)
  - DPP and carbon accounting systems
  - Ground and infrastructure assets (containers, CO₂ capture, etc.)
- Anchor points for MMIP capsules and DPP IDs related to wing components

This bucket does **not** own structural design or certification content; those remain under:

- `57-00_WINGS_GENERAL` – global lifecycle skeleton  
- `57-20_Subsystems` – per-subsystem lifecycle (flaps, spoilers, ailerons, etc.)

Instead, **57-30_ANCHORS** provides a **horizontal view** across those structures, focused on sustainability and traceability.

---

## 3. Internal Structure

The internal structure of this bucket is **design-driven** and intentionally flexible.

### 3.1 Design-Driven Principles

- Organize contents according to how systems are **conceived, designed, operated, and retired**, not by a rigid 01–14 skeleton.
- Use **57-30-XX_DESCRIPTION** IDs to group related concerns:
  - `57-30-01_Wing_Energy_Harvesting.md`
  - `57-30-02_Circular_Materials_and_LCA.md`
  - `57-30-03_Wing_DPP_and_Traceability_Links.md`
  - `57-30-04_ReUse_ReCycle_Strategies.md`
  - `57-30-05_Ground_and_Infra_Interfaces.md`

### 3.2 No Lifecycle Duplication

- Do **not** recreate the full 01–14 lifecycle here.  
- Instead, maintain the link to lifecycle phases via:
  - Cross-references to 57-00 and 57-20 documents
  - Metadata in headers (e.g. “Lifecycle tags: [Design, Operations, End-of-Life]”)
  - Central indexes (e.g. `57-30-99_ANCHORS-CROSS-INDEX.md`)

### 3.3 Suggested Sub-Buckets for ATA 57

- **57-30-01_Wing_Energy_Harvesting**  
  - Structural PV, thermal gradients, aeroelastic harvesting, etc.
- **57-30-02_Circular_Materials_and_LCA**

author: copilot
body:
Identified and fixed several performance inefficiencies in the training loop and supporting utilities.

### Changes

- **`optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)`** — Avoid zeroing gradients; setting to None is faster and more memory-efficient

- **`SmoothedValue.avg` O(n) → O(1)** — Track window sum/count incrementally instead of iterating the deque on every call

- **Cache `is_schedule_free_optim()` per epoch** — Avoid repeated type checks in the inner training loop

- **Early break in `collect_bn_stats()`** — Exit loop when sample limit reached instead of continuing to iterate

- **SAM `_grad_norm()` batched computation** — Use `torch._foreach_norm()` instead of individual `.norm()` calls:
  ```python
  # Before: individual norms + stack
  grad_list = [p.grad.norm(p=2).to(device) for p in params if p.grad is not None]
  norm = torch.norm(torch.stack(grad_list), p=2)

  # After: batched foreach operation
  norms = torch._foreach_norm(grads)
  norm = torch.linalg.vector_norm(torch.stack(norms))
  ```

- **`get_param_groups()` single-pass** — Iterate parameters once instead of twice with separate filter conditions

body:
Fix for incorrect gLabel routing, and new custom map implemented

Alternate label routing can no longer be used due to updates that happen within gLabel functions in some cases. Such as A_EventInfo -> Info. There are other issues caused by Alternate label routing as well.

Also, the benefits for using gmAltLabel map are no longer valid after the new label/func relationship handling, so it is dead weight. I did not yet remove all references to gmAltLabel just in case I am unaware of any problems the removal may cause with further testing. The map just remains inactive/dormant at the moment in case it needs to be reimplemented by simply removing a single comma.

This update also introduces a custom map that has case-sensitivity disabled by default. I have updated all maps within the project to use this new Map. Use of this new Map eliminates the need to follow every Map declaration with a 'caseSense:=0' setting change.

Added commit to prevent ampersand from being added to params that are numbers for DllCall and ByRef conversions. Also no longer adds the symbol to this.X (for ByRef). Will still need to provide a solution for this.X param in the future.

Also a reset tweak to a shared map in GuiAndMenu.

These are all minor tweaks I have been meaning to address, but keep forgetting about. So I thought I would push them at once.

author: etiennebacher
body:
This was undetected because I often tested on dirty repos with `--allow-dirty`, which took a fast path in `check_version_control()`. On a couple of test packages (dplyr, polars), `jarl check . --fix --with-timing` takes at least 4-5x less time.

The problem was that for each file, I was discovering the repo, getting the statuses of all files, and checking if any of those was dirty. Getting the statuses of all files in a repo is very expensive, so this was extremely slow in projects with a lot of R files. Now, I group paths by repo and then check the statuses once per repo only.

This also adds tests for cases where Jarl is called from a path with multiple subdirs that don't have the same VCS status.

## Description

Implements automatic shard discovery to enable comprehensive monitoring across all shards where the bot operates. Previously, monitoring was limited to a single shard configured via `SCREEPS_SHARD`, creating blind spots when the bot expanded to additional shards.

**Related Issues:** Closes #1528

### New: Shard Discovery Service (`packages/utilities/scripts/lib/shard-discovery.ts`)
- `discoverBotShards()` queries `/api/user/rooms` to find all shards with active rooms
- 5-minute caching to reduce API load

const discovery = await discoverBotShards();
// { shards: [{ name: "shard3", rooms: ["E54N39"] }], totalRooms: 1, discoveredAt: "..." }

The current monitoring and stats collection infrastructure operates on a single shard defined by `SCREEPS_SHARD` environment variable. This prevents comprehensive monitoring when the bot operates across multiple shards, leading to incomplete telemetry and blind spots in multi-shard deployments.

**Current Limitations:**
- Stats collectors query only the configured shard (`SCREEPS_SHARD`)
- Monitoring workflows lack awareness of which shards the bot actually occupies
- No mechanism to discover all shards where the bot has active rooms
- Multi-shard expansion requires manual workflow configuration updates

**Impact:**
- Incomplete telemetry when bot expands to additional shards
- Missed performance metrics and health alerts on non-primary shards
- Strategic planning operates with partial visibility
- Manual coordination required for multi-shard monitoring

## Proposed Changes

Implement a shard discovery mechanism that queries all shards where the bot has active rooms before collecting stats and telemetry.

### 1. Shard Discovery Service

Create `packages/utilities/scripts/lib/shard-discovery.ts`:

```typescript
interface ShardInfo {
  name: string;
  rooms: string[];
}

interface ShardDiscoveryResult {
  shards: ShardInfo[];
  totalRooms: number;
  discoveredAt: string;
}

/**
 * Discover all shards where the bot has active rooms
 */
async function discoverBotShards(api: ScreepsAPI): Promise<ShardDiscoveryResult> {
  // 1. Query /api/user/overview to get room list
  // 2. Parse room names to extract shard information
  // 3. Group rooms by shard
  // 4. Return structured shard list with room details
}
```

### 2. Update Stats Collection

Modify `packages/utilities/scripts/collect-ptr-stats.ts`:

```typescript
// Before collecting stats
const shardInfo = await discoverBotShards(api);
console.log(`Discovered ${shardInfo.shards.length} shards with ${shardInfo.totalRooms} rooms`);

// Collect stats from each shard
for (const shard of shardInfo.shards) {
  console.log(`Collecting stats from ${shard.name} (${shard.rooms.length} rooms)...`);
  const stats = await fetchResilientTelemetry(api, shard.name);
  // Aggregate or save per-shard stats
}
```

### 3. Update Monitoring Workflow

Enhance `.github/workflows/screeps-monitoring.yml`:

- Add shard discovery step before stats collection
- Pass discovered shard list to subsequent steps
- Aggregate multi-shard telemetry into unified reports
- Generate per-shar

## Summary

Complete v0.3.3 release with API completeness features: distributed tracing, performance monitoring, complete audit trails, and warnings infrastructure. All critical review findings addressed and ready for production.

**This PR consolidates:**
- PR #92: Critical fixes batch (10 issues)

- Tools: `build_catalog`, `search_catalog`, `get_catalog_summary`, `health_check`

**Performance Monitoring**
- Added `timing` metrics to all catalog/health operations

- `create_report`: Added `section_ids_added`, `insight_ids_added` arrays
